rationale: A legitimate and interpretable ablation of the archive's best performer (dropping the creditor term), though it sits close to the well-known net-payout/net-share-issuance anomaly and overlaps materially with CheapSelfFundedEquityBase, so the incremental information is the deflator-and-gate combination rather than the underlying construct.

This is CheapDeleveragingFromProfits with the denominator swapped from gross profit to cogs+xsga — same gate, same numerator, same NEG and winsorization — which is precisely the kind of cosmetic deflator variant the objective warns against, and the "decomposition" framing does not make a one-term denominator change a new mechanism.

Rescaling the winner's payload by total assets is another deflator swap rather than a new economic condition, and in that form ib−Δceq−Δdebt over assets is close to the published net-external-financing/free-cash-flow anomaly; the coverage argument is also weak since archive signals using cogs+xsga already reach 0.109 versus ~0.13 for asset-scaled ones.

The stated diagnostic ("does averaging strengthen the 3.5%/t=2.62 one-year result?") is not identified by this expression because it changes both the deflator (at instead of cogs+xsga) and the horizon simultaneously, so any difference cannot be attributed to smoothing, and absent that the proposal reduces to a routine MA(3) smoothing variant.

The option-on-the-enterprise argument is a genuine second economic condition rather than a threshold tweak, but the double gate leaves ~75% of the cross-section at exactly zero and the Δdebt term in the payload is mechanically correlated with the leverage screen, so portfolio stability and interpretation both need close scrutiny.

Substituting a flow-based cheapness gate for the balance-sheet gate is a defensible test of whether the mechanism requires book-value cheapness specifically, and it is not a rediscovery, though it remains a single-component swap and the prior sales-to-price gated signal in the archive performed poorly, tempering the prior.
